question: As an IMG preparing a patient for phacoemulsification cataract surgery, you are asked to instil mydriatic eye drops. Which combination is MOST appropriate for achieving maximal pupillary dilation prior to surgery?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The standard mydriatic regimen for cataract surgery combines: (1) Tropicamide 1% — anticholinergic, dilates and paralyses accommodation; (2) Phenylephrine 10% — alpha-agonist, stimulates dilator pupillae. Together they achieve maximal, sustained dilation. Instilled 30–60 minutes before surgery, repeated every 10–15 minutes × 3 doses.

Pilocarpine is a MIOTIC — it constricts the pupil. It is used post-operatively (e.g. after trabeculectomy) or in acute angle-closure, not for pre-operative dilation. Pilocarpine would directly oppose the desired mydriasis.
Timolol + dorzolamide lower intraocular pressure — they are anti-glaucoma agents with no mydriatic action. They may be used to control IOP spikes but are not pre-operative mydriatics.

Cyclopentolate is an anticholinergic mydriatic used mainly in children for refraction, not surgical mydriasis. For cataract surgery, the combination of an anticholinergic with a sympathomimetic (tropicamide + phenylephrine) provides superior, longer-lasting dilation.

overallFeedback.feedback: Mydriasis requires stimulating the dilator (phenylephrine, alpha-agonist) AND blocking the sphincter (tropicamide, anticholinergic). Pilocarpine causes miosis and must never be used before surgery.
Correct. Tropicamide 1% + phenylephrine 10% = the standard pre-op mydriatic pair. Anticholinergic + sympathomimetic → maximal dilation from two independent pathways.
